title: PyLockPeek
summary: Inspect a standardized pylock.toml offline and surface packages recorded without wheels.
problem: Developers need a quick way to understand what a generated pylock.toml contains before installing it, especially packages that only record source distributions.
audience: Python developers reviewing pylock.toml files in local, container, or CI workflows.
why_now: The pylock.toml standard was clarified in March 2026; current pip documents lock generation as experimental and uv still labels pylock installation support as preview.
difference: PyLockPeek does not resolve or install dependencies. It is a standard-library-only read-only view of an existing pylock.toml with a source-only artifact filter.
monetization_hypothesis: Best kept as a free local utility; a paid team reporting layer would need separate validation.
limitations: It does not evaluate environment markers or resolve dependencies.
A package with only an sdist recorded is not necessarily un-installable.

alternatives.name: pip lock
alternatives.difference: pip lock resolves and creates a lock file; PyLockPeek only reads an existing standardized lock.

alternatives.name: uv
alternatives.difference: uv can export and install pylock.toml; PyLockPeek is a zero-dependency read-only inspector.
